text: Yun Xiang is the mightiest champion beneath the Dragon Emperor. As one blessed and elevated by the Dragon Emperor, the hundred-odd men of the Heavenly Court's Palace Guard have defended the Imperial Road through storm and hardship for over a century. Even among these ever-selected heroes of Zhen Dan, Yun Xiang's peerless talent stands apart as heaven's chosen.
Divine Weapons of the Nine Provinces

Yun Xiang is the mightiest warrior beneath the Dragon Emperor. As an Ascendant blessed by the Dragon Emperor, the hundred-odd Palace Guards of the Heavenly Court have watched over the entire Royal Road through countless storms for over a century. As the Dragon Emperor's Champion, Yun Xiang acts in the Dragon Emperor's stead, wielding his grace and authority to cut down all manner of wickedness.
Yun Xiang commands the Heavenly Court's Palace Guard, Grand General of the God-Strategy Bureau. In weight of station, none save the Dragon and his Nine Sons can match him.
He summons the finest weapons of the realm, serving as the Dragon Emperor's vanguard, cutting through thorns and briars, giving his utmost in loyal service.

The Palace Guard are all heroes handpicked by the Dragon Emperor, already peerless among mortals, and further blessed by him — descending upon the battlefield like soldiers sent from heaven, unstoppable before all.
Beneath the high heavens, one still bears the Dragon's grace; with this mortal form, one walks alongside the Dragon.
The commander of the Palace Guard also oversees documents and administration; when necessary, he may directly govern the lands under the Heavenly Court in every direction.

As the situation grows ever more turbulent, dark currents stir beneath the celestial court, and some even believe it teeters on the edge of collapse. As the Dragon God's champion and Grand General of the God-Strategy Bureau, Yun Xiang has done all he believes possible to safeguard Zhen Dan's security. Yet his actions are seen by some Dragon-kin as overreaching, and the weight of his authority has even stirred wariness in [Jade Dragon] Yuan Bo.

Wherever Hao Tian's gaze falls, the wicked have no choice but to surrender their heads.

Yun Xiang glimpsed his own fate in a prophecy from the Astronomical Bureau: the Dragon God's chosen champion would fall beneath the blade of another chosen one, yet the Dragon God's palace would stand unbroken through the calamity. [Heaven's Favored] has prepared for this — so long as Zhen Dan can be preserved, no sacrifice is too great.
Yun Xiang is Grand General of the God-Strategy Bureau. The finest generals of the celestial court await his command, and the empire's most elite forces follow in his footsteps to crush the great foe.
Half of the Chang Yuan Tally. Only one who holds both halves may command the Chang Yuan Frontier Army.

The three passes have fallen, the nation lies in ruin, a thousand miles of fertile land reduced to wasteland. The lackeys of the Chaos Gods believe they have broken us, yet we still stand beneath the capital walls. Let our flesh and blood become the great rampart — for we are Cathay!

Guan Zi Mo is a heroine known throughout every household in Zhen Dan, and one of the rare few chosen maidens of the Moon Empress. Upon being granted a place among the Wind and Cloud Orchids, Guan Zi Mo received a revelation borne upon the veiled wind: Shang Yang already treads upon thin ice, and the shadow of chaos and ruin will arrive unbidden. In the Moon Empress's name, [Little Dragon Scale] would help the eighth-generation lord of Shang Yang weather the calamity and save the common people.

Guan Zi Mo is a heroine known to every household in Cathay, and one of the rare few chosen as Handmaidens of the Moon Empress. After being granted the honor of joining the ranks of Wind and Cloud Orchid, Guan Zi Mo received a revelation borne on the veiled wind: Shang Yang teeters on the brink of ruin, and the shadow of chaos and destruction draws near unbidden. In the name of the Moon Empress, the Little Dragon Scale shall help the Eighth-Generation Lord of Shang Yang weather this calamity and save the common people.

Guan Zi Mo has served Shang Yang for over three years, rooting out tyranny and comforting the good, hating evil as a mortal enemy. The people rely upon her without measure, calling her [Little Dragon Scale], the wandering knight of Sha Zhou.
When the frontier is in peril, however distant, she comes to its aid — crossing a thousand miles westward across the river, wholehearted and resolute, to serve the nation and save its people.

It is said in Shang Yang: when ten thousand armies are overturned, a figure in white robes appears amid the ranks, divine valor unmatched in the world — a heroine who proves herself the equal of any man.
Beneath the high heavens, one still bears the Dragon's grace; with this mortal form, one walks alongside the Dragon.

Though Guan Zi Mo is born a woman, her ambition rivals the heavens and her skill rivals mountains and seas — truly unmatched in this age. Though of mortal flesh, her will and strength are in no way inferior to those of Dragon-kin.

Though she wields supernatural power, she holds fast to a heart devoted to saving the world. In this age when chaos rises on every side and evil spirits run rampant, her white robes shine like the moon, cutting down every wicked path.
[The Campaign Robe is Stained Crimson, Soaking Through the Armor]
When the cold gleam flashes past, all who bear witness lose heart and courage, for they know full well what comes next...
Guan Zi Mo moves through vast armies as though through an empty land, unimpeded by any foe.
Cry of the Crane, Turning Clouds
When the cold gleam flashes past, all who watch will lose heart and courage — for they know full well what comes next...

Galloping a thousand miles, kicking up clouds of dust, fording rivers and scaling mountains as dark mist parts before it. Snapping the silken reins and shaking the jade tassels, its ink-dark shadow descends from the ninth heaven.
The divine weapons in Qiao Xiao's case are no mere ornaments.
Yan Kui's divine power infuses the weapons and armor nearby — allied blades become sharp enough to cut through iron like mud, while enemy armor crumbles at the slightest touch.

Zhao Qi's bond with nature surpasses common understanding — some claim to have witnessed her conversing with foxes, and it is upon this that they firmly believe her to be truly blessed by the Moon Empress.
So Long as the Moon Guards the People
Together We Lean on the Homeland's Light
One Bright Moon Over All the Seas

The Moonlight Sect led by Zhao Qi has spread rapidly along Cathay's eastern coast. They claim to have received revelation from the Moon Empress, and that they will lead the common people through the coming storm. Zhao Qi has even earned the backing of Ming Long herself — whether or not their doctrines are true, at least for now, they are truly bringing relief to the people.

A great many volunteers in Zhao Qi's army come from the coastal villages ravaged by Dark Elves in the east. 'The Moon Empress's gaze falls upon every child of Zhen Dan — so long as you are devout enough, her protection will surely come to you.'

According to her followers, the village where Zhao Qi lived as a child was mercilessly destroyed by Dark Elves. The Moon Empress brought her and other orphaned children back to the Heavenly Garden, forming the most recent generation of lunar disciples. Zhao Qi later left the celestial court and returned to Fu Zhou, her homeland, bringing the Moon Empress's blessing to its people. Now she serves as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed by Ming Long.

It is hard to imagine a Dragon-kin openly supporting a religious movement rising within her own domain, yet Ming Long has done exactly that — perhaps as a means to secure more support for herself, or perhaps at the Moon Empress's own bidding. Whatever the reason, the Moonlight Sect now enjoys full official backing across the eastern provinces.
Beneath the high heavens, one still bears the Dragon's grace; with this mortal form, one walks alongside the Dragon.

The Moonlight Sect has spread widely along Zhen Dan's eastern coast. Zhao Qi and her followers traveled south from Wei Jing, saving countless people of Zhen Dan along the way. They gather beneath the banners of moonlight, bathed in its sheltering glow — together, the faithful of the Moonlight Sect shall uphold Zhen Dan.
The whispers of trees, the calls of spirit beasts — Zhao Qi's extraordinary bond with nature has saved the common people's fragile uprisings time and time again.
When the realm rises or falls, every common man bears responsibility.

Xin Qi is the descendant of Zhen Dan's legendary hero Xin Wu, and the world says her martial prowess surpasses even his in every respect.
Drawing the Bow to Shoot the Sun
Loyal Servant of the Hao Court

Xin Qi is a descendant of the legendary Cathayan hero New Wu, and she has inherited her ancestor's martial prowess. After entering service, she was attached under Dong Yan, the Pacification Commissioner of Shang Yang, and was quickly appointed Cavalry Commandant for her distinguished feats in battle. Later, when Dong Yan led the gentry rebels in revolt, Xin Qi conspired with Ye Sheng and Feng Yao to kill him. Afterward, the two men seized Dong Yan's position and continued the rebellion themselves; Xin Qi, refusing to be complicit, fought desperately and narrowly escaped with her life. In recognition of her loyalty, Zhao Ming appointed her General Who Inspires Awe and ennobled her as Marquis of New Wu.

Xin Wu was a highly controversial figure — some regard his story as tragic and stirring, others as tyrannical and excessive, yet none can deny his battle prowess, which seemed almost supernatural. As the descendant of such a complex figure, Xin Qi has inherited both his martial valor and the controversy that surrounds his name.

Nearly everything about Xin Qi's current standing owes to her martial valor. After slaying Dong Yan, Ye Sheng and Feng Yao immediately led the rebels to surround Xin Qi and her followers within the palace hall, intending to eliminate them all. In this deadly standoff of one against a hundred, though dozens of guards fell in the fighting, Xin Qi alone fought her way out through sheer martial skill and escaped with her life.

Xin Qi possesses astonishing arm strength and excels with the longbow, drawing a bow of ten jun with ease. Wielding the divine bow Passing Wind of Beauty, her arrows bury themselves to the feathers. Her followers, trained under her example, have gained much from her tutelage as well.
Beneath the high heavens, one still bears the Dragon's grace; with this mortal form, one walks alongside the Dragon.
Fighting alone, her strength matches a thousand pounds.
Betrayed twice over, Xin Qi has repeatedly faced deadly peril, yet her loyal heart remains unshaken as she safeguards the Vast Dragon.
Unlocks skill: 'Cinnabar Shadow Breaks the Sky'

Dragon's stride, tiger's gait, its mane like flame, its neigh shaking the heavens like thunder. Iron hooves trample the enemy ranks to pieces, as the painted halberd dances and pierces the very heart of the sky.
Flying arrows pierce the clouds, breaking the silence
Flying arrows fall like rain upon the Celestial River
The blazing arrows have already left the bowstring — as beautiful and deadly as the master reborn from their flames.
Zhen Dan has produced heroine after heroine, who defend hearth and home alongside its sons and are remembered no less in history's annals.
Xin Qi moves through the battlefield like a spirit of death — any who dare challenge her will pay dearly for it.

As Zhu Long's most trusted mortal servant and foremost of the Twenty-Eight Generals' Stars, Duan Wei holds the vital post of Grand General of the Right Martial Marquis Guard in Ling Nan, commanding the Three Armies and overseeing the Beacon Watch.

'With Nan Ling at peace, Li Dao held a grand feast for the three armies, rewarding the meritorious officials and naming the Twenty-Eight Generals' Stars, declaring: "The hearts of you all stand as unmovable as mountains; with such stars accompanying me, what can a million enemies do against me!" Duan Wei's achievements were among the very greatest, guarding his lord with distinction. Zhu Long relied upon him as her right hand — sharing carriage when going forth, sharing seat when returning — and named him First Beneath the Dragon among all the star-generals.'
Triple Triumph of the Long Ge

Duan Wei led his army south, finally catching up with the main serpentfolk host in the great serpent rainforest, and led his men to strike with weapons raised. Though the enemy horde was broken, reinforcements soon arrived. Even deep in hostile territory, Duan Wei adapted to the battle in an instant, perceiving the moment of victory, using terrain and timing to his advantage, and unleashing sudden and ingenious stratagems. Though the enemy numbers were great, he won three battles in three engagements. Zhu Long rejoiced greatly: "In this dire strait of being outnumbered and surrounded on all sides, to witness your extraordinary valor and masterful strategy—Heaven surely aids my great cause through you!"
Double Swing of the Mighty Whip

The monkey bandits came from all directions, scheming to surround and slay him, yet Duan Wei drew his whip and charged forth, cutting them down all the way, beheading over a hundred. None of the monkey horde dared stand against him, and they scattered like startled birds and beasts.

As Zhu Long's most trusted general, Duan Wei is unstoppable on the battlefield. Though the generals of the various provinces have never formally measured themselves against one another, Zhu Long believes no mortal warrior in all of Grand Cathay surpasses Duan Wei in strength. As the General of the Right Martial Marquis, entrusted to hold his own front, Duan Wei has wrought miracle after miracle across his long military career, and his talent for commanding and disciplining troops has saved countless soldiers from needless sacrifice.

Martial virtue upon him, he plucks out the root of calamity with his own hand, sweeping away the murk and gloom; loyal to his sovereign and upholding righteousness, his achievements and fame complete, his glory shines through the Gate of Heaven.

The Sentinels have stood for over seventy years, yet Duan Wei has led them for barely a decade. The Vermilion Bird's transcendent guardians were reluctant at first to accept this man of common mortal stock, but Duan Wei has proven time and again that even set against the Imperial Guard, the Vermilion Bird, or even the Dragon God himself, a mortal can be every bit as great.

Scorching Waves Set the Sky Ablaze
The Flowing Fire Jade Lion is a blessed sacred beast, striding like a tiger through the southern frontier, burning away all wickedness.

Beyond the Celestial Mountains dwell countless xenos races that never fail to astonish the people of Grand Cathay, and among these, the more reasonable and cooperative peoples—such as the Tiger-folk and Monkey-folk—often maintain closer ties with Cathayans, even holding significant positions within the armies of the southern provinces.

Duan Wei is Li Dao's most trusted commander, sharing his carriage when they travel and his seat when they dine. His position as second only to Li Dao in Ling Nan has made him proud and arrogant, weighed down by his own accomplishments, and though the decisions of the [Duke of Pacified South] have always proven correct in the end, his fierce and unyielding temperament has earned him countless enemies, with political rivals lurking on every side. Zhu Long harbors a quiet unease—out of his sight, will this unstoppable warrior one day fall at the hands of his own people?

The Han clan of Nan Yang has long been a Soul-Enthralling noble house, beloved by the great families of the realm. When the Chaos of the Dragons erupted and the northern provinces were engulfed in war, Han Cheng led his army south to quell the rebellion. Unexpectedly, the rebels had already infiltrated close to home—the Dragon-kin themselves harbored treachery in secret. As the rebels seized territory from without, kin of dragon blood took up arms from within, and the city fell, suffering ten days of slaughter from which not even the Han clan was spared. The Celestial Court, already wary of Han Cheng, punished his faction for the loss of the city. Though they intended to eradicate his line root and branch, the outcry of injustice forced them to merely demote him to a minor clerk, installing another in his place. Yet Han Cheng retained the trust of the people and his merits only grew—all of Nan Yang, high and low, held him in deep regard. Though stripped of his rank, one call from him would summon a hundred in answer. Years passed, and the realm knew peace; for over a decade Han Cheng served faithfully at his post. That he now dredges up old grudges to declare himself king and stir rebellion—what a bitter lament this is!

The Han clan of Nan Yang has long been soul-enthralling nobility, beloved by the great houses. Han Cheng was granted the title of Duke of the Soul-Enthralling for his outstanding merits. But during the Dragon-Kin civil war, the northern provinces suffered greatly in the chaos of war—the Soul-Enthralling city fell, and the principal members of its great families were beheaded as a warning to others. Han Cheng, leading his army abroad, escaped this calamity. Now he has raised arms in rebellion and proclaimed himself Prince of Nan Yang. Some say this is an unforgivable blood feud; others say it is all a scheme of Sovereign Qing Bao.

In his youth, Han Cheng inherited his father's rank and was appointed a commandant, later rising through his own formidable martial skill to the post of General Who Inspires Awe, striding unchallenged across the battlefield and commanding Nan Yang with a tiger's tread—every soldier under him held him in reverent fear.

'Zhen Dan has stood for ten thousand years, yet all its ages have shared but one bloodline. I too once listened and believed this. But the sons and grandsons of dragons think only of their own gain, sowing discord until the Nine Sons warred among themselves and the mountains and rivers broke asunder. My own kin perished for it. Fortunately, the Sovereign Qing Bao revealed himself to me and gave me counsel—must the blood of dragons forever hold dominion?'
Han Cheng has already prepared himself, even should he have to stand alone against the entire Celestial Court.

Cathay has endured for over ten thousand years, and all its generations have shared one lineage. I too have heard and believed it, but the sons and grandsons of the dragon think only of their own gain, fostering discord until it came to the strife of the nine sons, and the shattering of mountains and rivers—my own family perished because of it. Fortunately, the Sovereign Qing Bao appeared to enlighten me: are the dragon's descendants truly of such stock? All present know the man I am—laboring to the utmost, only to end in a broken home and a dead family. Can this truly be called the righteous path? Today I have gathered you all here, to set the world aright and deliver its countless people!
Holding Power by Force of Arms

As Duke of the Soul-Enthralling line, Han Cheng already commands a mighty host, and with the lords of Nan Yang now rallying to his great cause, he need only await the tens of thousands more who will flock to his banner to sweep across the Nine Provinces.
[For those brimming with courage, the stronger the foe, the fiercer the fighting spirit it kindles.]

The whispers of Sovereign Qing Bao stir every nerve in Han Cheng's body, the crimes of the dragon's sons endlessly read aloud in his mind—the Way of Ten Thousand Changes has revealed the truth of the world!

Han Cheng has heard the Vast Heaven's transmitted voice, and the conspiracy of Sovereign Qing Bao has been laid bare in full. The Dragon Emperor is willing to forgive his deceived subjects—there is still a chance to return to the righteous path

During the civil war, Han Cheng's outstanding military talent swept aside the warlords of Yan Bin Plain, the Capital Circuit, and Xuan Yuan on behalf of the Celestial Court, and he repeatedly led reinforcements to aid the God-Strategy Bureau's pacification forces. At the Battle of Ming Zhu, he seized the secondary capital through a feint of striking east while attacking west; at the Battle of Hai Qi, he drowned the allied rebel and Dark Elf forces and slew the [King of Xuan Yuan] Ying Qie; at the Battle of Zhi Zhu, he lured the enemy with a Five-Army Formation and shattered the [Lord of the Jade Cauldron], ultimately forcing him to cut his own throat at the Yu River.

After Han Cheng marched to war, the Soul-Enthralling stronghold was left in the care of the Dragon-kin. Though the northern front saw constant fighting, this great city at the heart of Yan Bin Plain lay far from the frontlines and was garrisoned by the Celestial Court's proud Sky Junk Fleet—so when the rebels, aided by spies in matching blue Daoist robes hidden within the city, threw open the gates from within, the nobles still reveled in songs and dance.\\n\\nThe most valiant of the Dragon-kin were assassinated simultaneously, for the treacherous Dragon-kin among them were themselves the architects of this rebellion. Frenzied cultists, moving to the sound of an inscrutable sermon, slaughtered the loyalist generals within the government halls, and the leading members of the great families were all beheaded as a warning to others. Only those generals stationed in the industrial districts managed to escape with their lives, rescued by the Sky Junk Fleet. Though the God-Strategy Bureau's forces retook this vital city with the utmost speed, when Han Cheng and his unstoppable army returned to their homeland, all that met their eyes was a field of ruins.
No Crack Too Small to Slip Through
Pools of Wine, Forests of Meat
No one in Shang Yang can stop Ye Sheng any longer. His armies have torn off their masks and now plunder the common folk openly, while Ye Sheng and his lackeys sit atop a throne of blood.

Though the Ogre Wars ended long ago, great numbers of ogres still band together with the tribes of Zhen Dan's western frontier to raid the empire. Ye Sheng, gifted with extraordinary political skill, was chosen to suppress the unrest, and his string of victories in the west proved he was no mere manipulator of intrigue. The Bin Xi court thus named him General Who Breaks the Caitiffs, and he was granted command of troops to guard the frontier. Later, when Dong Yan led the treacherous gentry in rebellion, Ye Sheng at once marched his troops back to Shang Yang. After the siege, Ye Sheng, Xin Qi, and Feng Yao together plotted the death of the usurper Dong Yan, and the three swore an oath to jointly hold the Shang Yang court until the Eighth-Generation Lord of Shang Yang returned north to reclaim the throne. Yet Ye Sheng's ambitions did not end there—through his enticement, Feng Yao joined him in surrounding and killing Xin Qi, who refused to take part in a second rebellion. Now Ye Sheng holds Shang Yang by force, scheming to seize control of the entire western provinces of Zhen Dan and carve out his own kingdom.
Clearly, a man like Ye Sheng will stop at nothing to protect himself.

Though Ye Sheng seized this city by exploiting the power vacuum in Shang Yang, Zhao Ming will return one day. We cannot truly hope to bring down a Dragon-kin by ourselves—but fortunately, we still have many friends we can count on...
Shang Yang has become Ye Sheng's own miniature Celestial Court, and his hounds will ensure his reign of terror leaves no crack unfilled.

Once certain men cross their own moral threshold, there is no telling where they will stop. Ye Sheng's path to power has been paved with slaughter and conspiracy. His infiltration of Shang Yang runs to the very marrow — his sworn retainers and hidden assassins are scattered through every mansion in the city, and even the Hong Wu Overseers, the God-Strategy Bureau's own agents stationed in Shang Yang, have become his private killers. Until Zhao Ming's wrath finally reaches him, it seems nothing can stand in the way of his greater ambitions.
'Burn it! Take their wealth and their people, then reduce these worthless wretches and their city alike to ash. Let others know the fate of those who defy me.'
Ye Sheng's eyes and ears cover all of Shang Yang; those who oppose him have long since vanished into corners no one dares speak of.
Ye Sheng never worries about supplies—so long as common folk remain in a region, there is always more to squeeze from them.
Immortal March of War, Jade Spirit Breaks the Foe
The Brave Die, Yet Jade Bones Live On
The Death of Nong Chang, the Rebirth of Nong Chang

No one can say for certain where the Jade Blood Curse first arose, but this sudden nightmare has, over long ages, corroded the once-fertile Nong Chang Basin. Most survivors have withdrawn from this land, but some have chosen to keep fighting on the soil that raised them—Jin Xiao and the Jade Stone Guard are their last protectors.

When the Curse of the Jade Blood Clan descended upon the Nong Chang Basin, Jin Xiao, leader of the Protector Guard, could not escape the nightmare of undeath. Perhaps it was his unyielding will, his constitution beyond ordinary men, or perhaps mere luck, but as his flesh turned to bone, Jin Xiao managed to preserve his mind whole, and wearing the mask of the Protector Guard, he continued to lead Nong Chang's survivors against the Jade Blood Clan. With the arrival of the Jade Dragon, the crisis in Nong Chang was temporarily averted, but Jin Xiao's secret was also laid bare before the Jade Dragon. Rather than the death Jin Xiao had resigned himself to, Yuan Bo used his mighty sorcery to transform Jin Xiao's body—his shattered bones became jade, and the power contained within left Jin Xiao himself in disbelief. The Jade Dragon then rode off elsewhere as always. Jin Xiao does not know whether the Jade Dragon's act stemmed from trust, pity, or mere curiosity, but regardless, Jin Xiao will not waste this second life given to him.
Strictly speaking, Jin Xiao has been dead for a long time, but these jade bones bring vivid life-force to his broken body—perhaps even stronger than when he lived.
Jade Blood Stains the Collar, Jade Bones Interlace

Jin Xiao may be the one who has resisted the Jade Blood clan longer than anyone else alive; the other resistors have either become wandering spirits themselves or long since been buried six feet under. Jin Xiao's curse has now become the foundation of his struggle against the undead, and having received the Jade Dragon's blessing, he is certain to channel this unstoppable power to lead the people of Nong Chang in unleashing their boundless wrath upon the Jade Blood clan.
In a hundred battles he casts aside his body, treating life and death lightly; his blade sweeps through drifting clouds, scattering jade-white sand.

When the curse of the Jade Blood Clan descended upon the Nong Chang basin, Jin Xiao, leader of the Jade Stone Guard, could not escape falling into the nightmare of undeath. Perhaps through sheer force of will, an unusually resilient constitution, or simply luck, Jin Xiao—his flesh turned to bone—managed to preserve his mind intact, and continued to wear the guard's mask to lead the survivors of Nong Chang against the Jade Blood Clan. With the arrival of the Jade Dragon, the crisis in Nong Chang was momentarily resolved, but Jin Xiao's secret was also laid bare before the Jade Dragon. Contrary to what Jin Xiao expected—to be put to death—Yuan Bo instead used his mighty sorcery to transform Jin Xiao's body, turning his ruined bones into jade, and the power contained within left Jin Xiao in disbelief. The Jade Dragon then flew off as usual to other places; Jin Xiao does not know whether this was born of trust, pity, or mere curiosity, but regardless, he will not waste this second chance at life.

Once-prosperous Nong Chang now lies in ruins. Though the Jade Stone Guard still holds fast in the capital, Jin Xiao understands they must reclaim their homeland swiftly, or before the endless Jade Blood clan can fully engulf this shattered city, the lost survivors will crumble even within their own high walls.

Ling Nan is among the most perilous territories in the entire Celestial Court. The watchfires along the border sway uncertainly beneath the onslaught of foreign tribes, and countless casualties continually gnaw at the strength of the frontier prefectures. In such a harsh environment, the court of Zhu Long has cultivated a fierce martial spirit—countless rising stars have shone briefly here before falling, and only a rare few rise above the rest. In this southern frontier unprotected by the Great Wall, they make of their own bodies a rampart, defending the Empire's border.

The Qin clan of Ling Nan is the most influential lineage south of Sheng Jiang, and a pillar of support for Li Dao's rule, having served Zhu Long faithfully for a hundred years. Qin Yuan Yi's father, Qin Wen Cheng, was during his lifetime a renowned minister of the south whom Li Dao relied upon as his right hand. Now Qin Yuan Yi himself is one of the most decorated generals in Li Dao's court.
A hundred stratagems unleashed, the enemy broken across a thousand li.

The Qin clan of Ling Nan is the most influential family south of the Sheng River and a pillar of support for Li Dao's rule, having served Zhu Long faithfully for a hundred years. Qin Yuan Yi's father, Qin Wen Cheng, was in his lifetime one of the great southern ministers upon whom Li Dao relied most heavily, and Qin Yuan Yi himself is now one of the most decorated generals in Li Dao's court.
It is believed that Qin Yuan Yi's soul carries a fragment of the primal spirit of Zhen Dan's Sovereign beast, and that it will manifest itself in moments of grave crisis.

The Qin clan of Ling Nan is the most powerful lineage south of the Sheng Jiang river, and a pillar of support for Li Dao's rule, having served Zhu Long faithfully for a hundred years. Qin Yuan Yi's father, Qin Wen Cheng, was in his time a renowned minister of the south whom Li Dao relied upon as his right hand — and now Qin Yuan Yi himself is one of the most decorated generals in Li Dao's own court.

'Where the cold blade flashed, blood splattered—the rebel chief Yun Zhao fell from his saddle. Before the fifteenth clash was done, his spear had already unhorsed the He Dong tyrant Li Yun Zhao. Guo Shao charged in with his lance; Yuan Yi's spear swept it aside and countered with a reverse thrust. The Wu brothers both leveled their spears to join the fray, three weapons converging as one—yet General Qin, spirit undaunted, wove his spearplay: left to parry the Bin iron mace, right to sweep aside the Yun Lu blade, straight for Guo Shao's face. Facing three at once, he remained utterly composed; wherever his spear pointed, none of the three dared draw near. The battle raged until the sun grew dim and the forest wind moaned in grief, his war robe stained crimson with blood, his crest in disarray—and the ten myriad soldiers of He Dong were struck with terror!'
It is believed that a fragment of the primordial spirit of Cathay's Sovereign Beast resides within Qin Yuan Yi's soul, manifesting itself in moments of dire crisis.

Qin Yuan Yi and Duan Wei each guard one end of the canal, standing like the Door Gods that the people of Zhen Dan paste upon their doors to ward off evil, holding the threats to Zhen Dan at bay beyond the mountains and forests.

The primal spirit of the Sovereign beast is a burden no mortal should be able to bear, one that should have long since claimed Qin Yuan Yi's life. Yet he has endured this struggle against fate to this very day, and has turned that burden to his own use.

Descriptions of Hou Qian vary greatly across the legends of different regions. In the songs of the north, he is a bloodthirsty, raging great ape. In the tales of western storytellers, he is a creature resembling a baboon, with beautiful golden fur and a swollen red rear—for the Monkey King is forever in a fury. In the legends by the eastern shore, this enormous ape has an astonishing appetite, his bare belly covered in unsightly boils. To some in the south, the Monkey King is instead a slight spider-monkey, leaping from shoulder to shoulder among allies and enemies alike, his words a mixture of truth and lies.
[Guardian of the Heavenly Gate] Hou Qian

As Warden of Heaven's Gate, Hou Qian commands a hundred thousand Dragon Guards of Wei Jing. He is the Dragon-kin most trusted by Yuan Bo, and a general held in high esteem by Yun Xiang as well — it is through his mediation that these two, otherwise at daggers drawn, manage to maintain a delicate balance.

Above the Heavenly Court, the Dragon Emperor's Guard stand silent watch outside the palace of the Vast Heavens, and only their leader travels back and forth to the God-Strategy Bureau. Since the War of Soul-Enthralling, the Dragon Emperor's Guard have repeatedly drawn back the boundaries of their watch, ceding more of Wei Jing's city defenses to mortals, while the vast Heavenly Court Dragon Guard was summoned to the capital to form a new formation. Hou Qian arrived as merely one dragon-kin among many, but now, having earned glorious battle merit time and again, he stands as the Guardian of Wei Jing, commanding a hundred thousand dragon guards.
Search the Mountains, Subdue the Demons

Grand Cathay is a realm brimming with the Winds of Magic, and all things in it gather spiritual energy—some of which, over long ages, transform into malevolent things that plague the land. Most of the time, local officials or Buddhist and Daoist practitioners are enough to settle such matters, but sometimes a great demon stirring up chaos cannot be tolerated even by the soldiers of the God-Strategy Bureau. At such times, Hou Qian leads the Heavenly Court's divine troops to subdue demons and banish evil.
Slay the Flood Dragon, Still the Waves

Like the dragon-horses and the qilin, the flood dragons are an ancient bloodline of the dragons, yet despite their close resemblance to true dragons, their uncontrollable fury made them intolerable to the dragon-kind, and so they were banished to slumber beneath lake depths. Some flood dragons, over long ages, mastered their tempers and came to guard territories for the dragons, while the rest, consumed by resentment, became malevolent spirits, their unfathomable rage raging alongside floods and disasters. By the riverbank of Hou Qian's hometown, a stone tablet records this history: "The province had a flood dragon; whenever the river swelled, it rode the flood to wreak havoc, sweeping away homes, and countless people drowned—none were said able to subdue it. Then Hou Qian took up his sword and entered the water, slaying the flood dragon as it emerged, its blood staining the river's heart, ending the people's suffering. Its sinews and bones were forged into a hilt, its three heads into blades—thus was made the Trident-Edged Double-Bladed Saber."
Wise Eyes Gaze Upon the World

Hou Qian was born with a Heavenly Eye that can see through every disguise and illusion, discerning the true nature of all things. When the Changeling transformed into Yun Xiang and strode boldly into the God-Strategy Bureau, it was Hou Qian who saw through its disguise at a single glance.

It is said that after the Monkey King's army was defeated and fled south, Hou Qian, under Yun Xiang's orders, led fifty thousand celestial soldiers of the capital together with an allied dragon-kin force in pursuit of the bandit. Riding the clouds, Hou Qian rode alone at the vanguard and cornered the ape at Kun Lan Mountain. Had the Monkey King arrayed for open battle as he did in the War of Heavenly Court, it surely would have shaken heaven and earth once more, but this time he could afford no delay and could only scramble to respond in a panic. Hou Qian, already formidable in skill, fought even fiercer, driving the Monkey King back until his gleaming Trident-Edged Double-Bladed Saber left him scrambling to defend himself. Yet the ape-king's supernatural arts brought forth endless surprising tricks, and in the flash of an instant he even shook Hou Qian to his core. Seeing the situation turn dire, Hou Qian hastily drew forth the treasure gifted by the Old Immortal of Kun Shan and hacked fiercely at the ape-king's head, but the Monkey King dodged aside in a flash, leaving behind a shower of fur before vanishing entirely, leaving only the immortal axe behind, which had cleaved a great chasm through the surrounding mountains.
'One becomes ten, ten becomes a hundred, and the transformations of hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, millions — all are the arts of the Howling Celestial Hound.'
Great Sage of the Yellow Wind

A hundred years have passed since that day. Xin Wu has long since become a desolate ruin, the yellow sand still raging aimlessly across the land. Yet occasionally, bold merchants passing along the road claim to hear a clamor of voices rising from the ruins of Xin Wu—alas, obscured by the Yellow Wind, none can see clearly whether it is man or demon.

A hundred years have passed since that day, and Xin Wu has long lain desolate and uninhabited, the yellow sand still raging aimlessly across the land. Yet occasionally, bold merchants pass through that road, claiming the ruins of Xin Wu still echo with the clamor of voices—though obscured by that yellow wind, none can say clearly whether it is man or demon
It learned every last one of the Old Immortal of Kun Lan's marvelous arts—what a sinful thing to do. One wonders what the old immortal above must think of this...

The Great Sage Yellow Wind seized Xin Wu, already possessing formidable magic, and with the skull of Xin Wu's fallen general fashioned into an implement of power, it briefly held dominion unrivaled, drawing demons and monsters from every direction to recognize it as their Great Sage.

That fateful gale over Xin Wu once cost Zhao Ming the White Tiger and drove Miao Ying away from Xuan Wu, shaking the Three Realms and the Nine Provinces to their core. Even later, when the Monkey King marched north upon the Celestial Court, he made certain his simian kin stayed far, far away from this place.

Legend says the Great Sage Yellow Wind stole the skull of Xin Wu's great general to absorb the essence of heaven and earth, yet no matter how it cultivated, it could never attain true enlightenment. In its boundless fury, it destroyed the city of Xin Wu, and after a hundred more years of cultivation, it descended into madness, bringing ruin wherever it went.

Ever since that gale swept over Xin Wu, the Celestial Court has sent countless armies to strike it down, yet the Great Sage Yellow Wind's own power is formidable, and its subordinates number among the fiercest of generals—locked in endless struggle with Zhen Dan's celestial soldiers. Compounded by the Yellow Wind Array that blots out the sun and sky, time and again Zhen Dan's great armies have returned empty-handed.

Xue Ding, [Son of the Yin River], is the Left Guardian Grand General of the Jade Court. He accompanied Yun Feng Zi on the campaign against Lu Si Qi Ya, clad in white robes, bearing his staff and talismans, charging into battle with a great roar, unstoppable wherever he went. Xue Ding has fought alongside the Jade Dragon for over twenty years, crushing the Nine Tribes of the wild orcs, subduing the Black Lotus bloodline, and breaking the lizardmen—his merits are many and great.
[Son of the Yin River] Xue Ding

Xue Ding plays a pivotal role in the Celestial Empire's foreign wars, appearing in nearly every battle. Countless formidable enemies who once scorned the Celestial Empire have been brought to their knees by his campaigns

For over twenty years he has fought alongside the Jade Dragon, crushing the savage orcs of the Nine Tribes, subduing the Black Lotus bloodline, and shattering the Lizardmen—his merits are manifold and renowned.

Xue Ding's fame has spread to every corner of the realm; he received the post of Master Instructor of the Cloud Banner Command from Yuan Bo, becoming one of the Thirty-Six Instructors of the Jade Court's forces.
Troops and horses fully assembled, ready to answer the call of the campaign.

Xue Ding is the Left Guardian General of the Jade Court. When he campaigns abroad, his glory is the Jade Court's glory, and his strength is the Jade Court's strength.\\n\\nHe will never allow the Jade Court to be shamed.
Heavenly Army of the Jade Court
Xue Ding commands the Jade Court's Left Army, tens of thousands of jade warriors awaiting his every command outside his tent, and he has already led this legion across the four seas.

Liu Yue Ru is the direct disciple of [Xuan Nv], the founder of the Xuan Heng Sect of Fu Zhou. After the Battle of Xuan Yuan, almost all the sect leaders perished. Though [Xuan Nv] narrowly survived, her six roots were shattered beyond hope of recovery. Liu Yue Ru and her fellow disciples fought to the death, and of the eight hundred students, only seven remained. With the sect brought to such ruin, [Xuan Nv] passed the sword technique down to Liu Yue Ru, that the Xuan Heng lineage might not vanish from the world. [Xuan Nv] was laid to rest on Mount Heng in Fu Zhou, and her surviving sisters scattered to the four winds—some perished in battle against the Dark Elves, others withdrew from the martial world. Now only Liu Yue Ru remains, having abandoned her empty mountain gate to wander the world, hunting down and assassinating Dark Elf nobles and officials wherever she finds them. The old tales have become mere talk over wine, but the world still remembers the name of the Sword of Severed Love.
[Sword of Broken Affection] Liu Yue Ru

Liu Yue Ru is the direct disciple of [Xuan Nv], master of the Xuan Heng sect of Fu Zhou. After the Battle of Xuan Yuan, nearly every sect master perished; though [Xuan Nv] narrowly survived, her six roots of perception were shattered beyond recovery. Liu Yue Ru and her fellow disciples fought to the death, yet of eight hundred students, only seven remained. With the sect reduced to such ruin, [Xuan Nv] passed her sword technique on to Liu Yue Ru, so that the Xuan Heng lineage would not vanish from the world. [Xuan Nv] was laid to rest on Heng Mountain in Fu Zhou, and her surviving sisters scattered to the four winds — some perished fighting Dark Elves, others retired from the martial world. Now only Liu Yue Ru remains, having abandoned the empty halls of her sect to wander the realm, hunting down and assassinating Dark Elf nobles wherever she finds them. The old tales have become mere idle talk — what remains in this world is only the name of the Sword of Severed Love.

Liu Yue Ru is the direct disciple of [Xuan Nv], and in a moment of desperate crisis was granted the Xuan Heng Sword Technique—the ultimate secret art passed down through a century of the Xuan Heng lineage now rests entirely within her.

At the martial world alliance, every sect claimed to be righteous and orthodox, yet when the fate of the nation hung in the balance, each harbored its own hidden agenda. While the Eight Great Sects hesitated, it was the Xuan Heng sect that first stepped forward to support Tang Jing Yin. Setting aside grand ambitions to serve the nation—if we call ourselves champions of the righteous path, how could we stand idle while the Dark Elves commit such atrocities? In this hour of crisis, we who bear this ultimate skill vow to restore clear skies to all under heaven.
Seven hundred and ninety-three disciples of the Xuan Heng sect died in a single day—the blood debt owed by the Dark Elves must be repaid twofold.
Aid the World, Pacify the People
'Never again shall such a tragedy be allowed to repeat itself. Not as long as I still draw breath.'

[Xuan Nv], in her final hour of peril, passed the Xuan Heng Sword Technique on to Liu Yue Ru. It is neither as domineering as the Roaring Suan Ni Blade Style nor as fierce as the Jade Wind Sword Technique, yet it holds infinite variation, advancing and retreating with perfect fluidity.\\n\\n[[col:green]]The Xuan Heng Sword Technique is profound beyond measure, and Liu Yue Ru has yet to fully grasp it even now. You may invest additional skill points into this ability to further master the Xuan Heng Sword Technique and gain corresponding stat bonuses.[[/col]]
Her sect has faded away along with those she once knew—she is now the last disciple of the Xuan Heng lineage.

One of the Three Heroes of Xing Po, deeply versed in the Dao, appearing sometimes in human form, sometimes as a raven—none can say for certain what his true form is. Once regarded with suspicion by the alchemist masters, his heart nonetheless remains devoted to the common people. Commanding the Raven-Feather Legion in service to the Moon Empress, he has rendered great service in protecting the nation and its people, and the Celestial Observatory relies upon him as a trusted right hand.
You hear the rustle of feathers, and can even feel the blade closing in on you, but where exactly is he?

Among the ministers who narrowly escaped that fateful night, rumors grew ever more exaggerated—they said the Raven Guard slit the throats of eighteen palace guards of the rebel king's court with nothing but a single feather. Was it truly just a feather, or a sword that can take the form of a feather? At the very least, the dead can no longer say.
[No Form to Find, No Shadow to Hide]

Not a few conspiracy theorists among Cathay's elite believe the Raven-Feather Guard has always been in collusion with the ratfolk who carry out their base deeds, for wherever the Raven-Feather Guard appears, ratfolk assassins are invariably found nearby. But they never consider that it might simply be because of the Raven Guard's presence that these highly skilled schemers are discovered at all.
Ku Xi is the leader and mentor of the Raven-Feather Guard of the Xing Po Imperial Guard, and a symbol of terror in the hearts of the heretics who lurk within Grand Cathay.
No one dares declare whether Master Ku Xi is truly man or raven, but everyone on the battlefield can hear the terrifying cry that surrounds him.
Though ten thousand forms of treachery and evil may arise, this blade shall cut them all down.
As founder of the Raven-Feather Legion, Ku Xi's skill is unmatched anywhere in Zhen Dan — a true grandmaster among assassins.
The Raven-Feather Legion serves the Moon Empress, even surpassing the Hong Wu Overseers of the inner palace in stealth and assassination—and every member of the Raven Guard trained under Ku Xi.
'The eyes of the Raven Guard see all...'

Silent as gods and spirits, swift as wind and thunder. Advancing, none can stand before him; retreating, none can pursue. Front and rear answer in concert, left and right move at his command. He shifts the nature of the Five Elements, alters the mandates of the four seasons. Is he man? Is he immortal? I cannot say—he is the purest brilliance among men.
Open, Rest, Life, Injury, Obstruct, View, Death, Fright—once the eight trigrams are unfurled, the enemy is overcome and victory secured.
A creation of the Heavenly Court, a miniature replica of the magnificent architecture of Wei Jing.
A general's warhorse is his most trusted and valiant companion. Just don't name it 'Little Daisy.'
Fang Wen Zi is gifted beyond measure, wielding the power of the Winds of Magic with consummate mastery—but his body has also grown frail from bearing a force beyond what mortals can withstand.

Fang Wen Zi is a senior Director of the Astronomical Bureau and one of the Three Heroes of Xing Po. After the Dragon Emperor and the Moon Empress devoted themselves to their secret plans, certain extraordinary individuals in the mortal world are always inspired to take crucial actions to help Zhen Dan avoid potential catastrophe—and now, the Moon Empress's chosen one is Fang Wen Zi.

Fang Wen Zi is a senior Grand Astronomer of the Celestial Observatory, and the one who conveys the will of the Moon Empress. After the Dragon Emperor and the Moon Empress devoted themselves to their secret plans, extraordinary individuals in the mortal world have always emerged, receiving their guidance and taking crucial actions to spare Zhen Dan from potential calamity. Now, the Moon Empress's chosen vessel is Fang Wen Zi.

Though Fang Wen Zi is a senior member of the Astronomical Bureau, he prefers to immerse himself in mountains and wilderness, feeling the spiritual breath of heaven and earth and refining his own character.
Fang Wen Zi plans with utter thoroughness, mastering every detail great and small; in matters of army and warfare, with a single step taken he has already calculated ten steps ahead.

During the Monkey King's rebellion, Fang Wen Zi received the Moon Empress's guidance and, representing the Jade Dragon's court, mediated among the dragon-kin of all quarters, debating and overcoming every dissenting voice through sheer eloquence, bringing about the alliance of dragon-kin to strike down the rebels. His mastery of strategy and unmatched gift for persuasion were beyond compare.

The classic texts compiled by Fang Wen Zi provide a reference for the operation of the Celestial Empire, allowing every detail of data from across the realm to be recorded and consulted in official documents.
Through a series of reforms, Fang Wen Zi weakened the grip of local strongmen on the grassroots economy, dissolving the economic blockages caused by corruption.
Having all things prepared before the march allows one to remain unshaken in the face of danger.
Every motion and breath, every fist and form, is already etched into the surging hot blood of Pei Yue.

Laughing at the world's petty grudges, raising a cup once more with heroic spirit; the Divine Fist rolls on, stirring Heaven's own wrath—we of this generation ascend the azure clouds with joyful abandon.                                                             [[col:white]]You do not need to allocate skill points to this skill—it will automatically level up as the character's level increases. When the character reaches level 50, all four of Pei Yue's attributes will receive a 20% bonus.[[/col]]

When Pei Yue steadies his breath and focuses his spirit, even the surrounding river's waters grow still beneath the pressure of his presence: he will use redirected force to reverse his enemy's assault, then return it in full.

Pei Yue has ascended to the very summit of martial arts; the heroes of Grand Cathay's martial world have all fallen before him, and among all the mountain peaks, he has no rival remaining. Perhaps, after all he has endured, the Martial Fanatic finally understands what constitutes true martial arts and true chivalry better than those who merely call themselves heroes.

In Pei Yue's heart, martial arts does not carry the many layered meanings that most Cathayan warriors ascribe to it. Martial arts is simply martial arts—hold fast to this path, and reach its very pinnacle.
Pei Yue's fist technique is so pure and unadorned that few of Grand Cathay's masters, with all their ever-changing forms, can withstand even a single exchange with him.

Pei Yue's life thus far has been an unending journey. He has traveled every inch of Zhen Dan, defeating one arrogant martial arts master after another in sect after sect, seeking the very limits of martial skill. Now, the Martial Fanatic has settled beneath the banner of Bin Long Men, seeking only to sweep aside every hero and champion of Shang Yang.

Pei Yue's life thus far has been one unending journey — he has traveled every corner of Zhen Dan, defeating the most arrogant masters of one school after another in his pursuit of martial perfection. Now the Martial Fanatic has settled beneath the Bin Long sect, seeking only to sweep aside every hero of the eight directions in Shang Yang.
Looking Down on the Western Desert
Those northern warriors who fancy themselves born for war charge forward with blade in hand, only to fall before his fists.
Countless schools line the southern bank of the Jade River, the birthplace of Zhen Dan's martial arts — yet not one among them can withstand the Martial Fanatic's fist.
Even in Shang Yang, where masters from all eight directions gather, Pei Yue still claims first place in the arena with ease.

[Martial Sage] has journeyed through Zhen Dan's long history for a hundred years. As a military commander from the same era as Xin Wu and a champion personally chosen by the Jade Dragon, blessed with a divine artifact bestowed by the dragons, [Martial Sage] was granted a lifespan as long as that of the Dragon Emperor's Guard, aiding the dragons in preserving Zhen Dan's peace and stability. All the soldiers who once fought beside him have long since faded away, and the common people of today can no longer recall this great warrior's true name—only the title of [Martial Sage] remains recorded in history.
[Sage of War] True Lord Ta Yu Zai Tian

The [Sage of War] has worn his imperially bestowed jade mask to guard Zhen Dan for a hundred years. The common people speak of him as an immortal protector of the nation, and villains and traitors alike tremble at the mere mention of his name.
Tempered by Time, Grown Ever Stronger
The peerless [Martial Sage], unmatched from birth, has grown ever stronger through a century of battles.

The title of Martial Sage has long been bound in the hearts of Cathayans to every noble virtue of the martial warrior; the common folk have even come to venerate him as an immortal—the True Lord Ta Yu Zai Tian.

The soldiers who once fought alongside him have long since scattered like dust in the wind, leaving only the [Martial Sage] to guard the nation's gate alone—and no matter how many enemies he faces, he never wavers.
Let Jade and Stone Burn Together
The [Martial Sage] will break the mask's hold over him, and his frozen life will flow once more.
Ten thousand ages of peace and stability, yet a new calamity arises, and the people suffer. Yet peace and harmony shall flow again, for righteous warriors will surely arise to quell the chaos.
Blade drawn, mounted for battle, he warms fresh wine; a single steed cuts through dust, breaking through three armies.

Ying Jin was renowned as a prodigy in Nan Yang since childhood, and as he grew older, his unstoppable talent shone ever brighter. After the Soul-Enthralling clan entered service, Ying Jin has always assisted the Duke of the Soul-Enthralling, personally attending to matters both great and small, earning the sincere admiration of the entire court.
Ying Jin is known to the people as the [Lord of Brocade Jade]. He is a talent renowned throughout the world, a minister without peer in this age.

Ying Jin was renowned as a prodigy in Nan Yang since childhood, and as he grew, his unstoppable talent shone ever brighter. Since Soul-Enthralling entered office, Ying Jin has served at his side without fail, personally attending to matters both great and small, earning the sincere admiration of the entire court.

Soul-Enthralling's sky junk technology is renowned throughout the world—so much so that even the peerless blind artisans of Nan Gau must regard Soul-Enthralling's engineers as rivals. These powerful war machines form a vital part of Soul-Enthralling's army, and under Ying Jin's command, they remain undefeated to this day.

Though Han Cheng and Ying Jin's friendship has endured for decades, they have come to an irreconcilable divide over the matter of the rebellion. Ying Jin listed countless reasons in his efforts to persuade Han Cheng, hoping to make him see the conspiracy behind these events, but it seemed some other force had seized control of his old friend's mind. Ying Jin's attempt failed, but he has no intention of abandoning his bewitched comrade. After much struggle, he chose to retreat into seclusion—if at all possible, he will exhaust every effort to bring Han Cheng back before matters become irreversible, and if there is no other way, he will also take up arms against the rebel king of Nan Yang for the sake of Grand Cathay's greater cause.
With but a single command from Ying Jin, a rain of fire blotting out the sky and sun answers his call.
Blazing fire lights up the heavens and illuminates the sea of clouds; masts and oars burn to ash and drift away.
Ying Jin commands his sky junk legion through the sound of his flute, each melody a symbol of a command.
Who understands the warrior's heart within the flute's melody? The riverside sands vainly illuminate the bones of those who marched to war.

The artisans of the Soul-Enthralling Lineage tirelessly pursue the achievements of the Blind Craftsmen and the Martial Artisans' Bureau day and night, and all their progress in sky junk technology has been fully applied to Ying Jin's fleet.
