Grand Chamberlain of the Jade Court

Yi Yao Hua is the elder sister of [Sky-Defying Sovereign] Yi Qing, who won great renown in the Third Northern Expedition. She also holds the illustrious post of Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in the Jade Court, serving both as the bond between the Jade Dragon and mortals, and as the messenger between the Heavenly Court and the Jade Dragon.

Yi Yao Hua is the elder sister of [Sky-Defying Sovereign] Yi Qing, who earned great renown in the Third Northern Expedition. She herself is the illustrious Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at the Jade Court — both the bond between mortals and Jade Dragon, and the messenger between the celestial court and Jade Dragon.
Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices

Yi Yao Hua is the elder sister of [Sky-Defying Sovereign] Yi Qing, who earned illustrious battle merit in the Third Northern Expedition, and is herself an eminent Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices of the Jade Court—both a bond between the Jade Dragon and mortals, and a messenger between the Heavenly Court and the Jade Dragon.

Every Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices is greatly revered by the people, and their arrival is regarded as a sign of favor bestowed by the Dragon Emperor and the Moon Empress upon that place.
Yi Yao Hua recites various invocations during rituals, conveying the wishes of the mortal world to the Vast Heavens.
Yi Yao Hua recites various invocations during rituals, conveying the wishes of the mortal world to the Vast Heavens.

The shamanistic Nuo culture of southern Grand Cathay can be traced back to the era when the Dragon Emperor first descended. The local people believe these traditional rituals can ward off calamity and dispel evil spirits, and some even use these rites to harm their enemies.

The people of Grand Cathay revere the resonance between Heaven and Man, offering sacrifices of various forms to seek the blessing of the Vast Heavens and the Dragon Emperor, and it falls to the Ministers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices of the various courts to preside over such rites.
Deputy Commander of the Imperial Guard

Miao Yi is Yun Xiang's deputy commander, and the only known female member of the Dragon Emperor's Guard. Nearly all of Zhen Dan's heroines destined to be remembered in history are chosen for the Moon Empress's court. Yet just as people believed Miao Yi too would be chosen as one of the Moon Empress's maidens for her great deeds, an emissary from the Heavenly Court summoned her instead in the name of Hao Tian, and Miao Yi thus became fortunate enough to be among the last to receive the Dragon Emperor's blessing. In the hundred years since the departure of the Vast Dragon, the Guard has fought and sacrificed itself countless times for the survival of Zhen Dan. To this day, fewer than a hundred of the Heavenly Court's Guard remain, but Miao Yi and her comrades will steadfastly uphold their ancient oath—true this autumn, and true for ten thousand generations to come.
Deputy Commander of the Imperial Guard

Miao Yi is Yun Xiang's deputy commander, and the only known female member of the Dragon Emperor's Guard. Cathay's heroines worthy of being recorded in history are usually chosen to serve in the Moon Empress's court, and when people believed that Miao Yi too would be chosen by the Moon Empress for her great achievements, an envoy from the Heavenly Court instead summoned her in the name of the Vast Heaven. Miao Yi thus had the fortune to become one of the last to be blessed by the Dragon Emperor. In the hundred years since the Vast Dragon's departure, the Palace Guards have fought and sacrificed themselves countless times for Cathay's survival. To this day, fewer than a hundred remain in the Heavenly Court's service, but Miao Yi and her comrades will steadfastly uphold their ancient oath—this autumn, as in all ages to come

Miao Yi is Yun Xiang's second-in-command, and the only known female member of the Dragon Emperor's Guard. Nearly all of Zhen Dan's history-making heroines are drawn into the Moon Empress's court—and just as people believed Miao Yi, too, would be chosen for her great achievements to join the Empress's ranks, an emissary from the Celestial Court instead summoned her in the name of Hao Tian himself. Miao Yi thus became fortunate enough to be among the last to receive the Dragon Emperor's blessing. In the century since Hao Long's departure, the Palace Guard has fought and sacrificed itself countless times for Zhen Dan's survival. To this day, fewer than a hundred of the Celestial Court's guard remain, yet Miao Yi and her comrades will unwaveringly uphold their ancient oath—true this autumn, and true for ten thousand generations to come.

To the mortal world, the Dragon Emperor's Guard is nearly a legend. In the age when the Dragon Emperor still walked among the living, the Guard's might was enough to lay flat any nation of the mortal realm. But as the Dragon Emperor and the Moon Empress devoted themselves wholly to their grand design, watchful enemies came pressing in from every side, and the Dragon Emperor's Guard could never again be replenished. Mortals can no longer see full formations of the Guard fighting on the front lines of the Celestial Court as they once did a century ago—but when these surviving legends descend upon the battlefield, the people of Zhen Dan witness myth and reality overlap.

The last time the Great Wall was utterly breached, an unprecedented Chaos legion swarmed into Zhen Dan: the colossal terracotta guardians of the Spirit Road collapsed within the Terracotta Warriors' mausoleum, the Soul-Enthralling stronghold was consumed by the falling Sky Junk Fleet, Miao Ying's legions clung to survival beneath the high walls, and Yuan Bo's Jade Stone Legion was lured astray by the schemes of the Sovereign Qing Bao. In this hour when Zhen Dan's very survival hung by a thread, the Dragon Emperor's Guard held back the onslaught of the Chaos alliance at the near-ruined Soul-Enthralling stronghold—nine Greater Daemons were banished, hundreds of Chaos Champions were struck down, and the vast legions following in their wake scattered like startled birds. When Miao Yi, having taken up the mantle of her fallen second-in-command, tallied the losses under Yun Xiang's orders, they realized: the age of the Dragon Emperor's Guard had come to an end. The unbearable losses had stripped them of their strength as a final trump card—though the surviving Guard remained powerful enough to shake all of Zhen Dan, these survivors were now but an echo of past glory.

Since the end of that last great battle, the Dragon Emperor's Guard did not leave the capital for a long time, until the outbreak of the civil war—as the situation grew increasingly uncontrollable, the Guard was dispatched to strip various generals of their authority, crushing those who defied their orders like ants underfoot. The damage the civil war inflicted upon Zhen Dan was contained in time, but it also bred distrust between the capital's Guard and Yuan Bo. Miao Yi, as Yun Xiang's deeply trusted deputy, was dispatched to the Jade Court to seek aid from the Celestial Court's chief minister, but Yuan Bo refused the God-Strategy Bureau's request: he had a mission he was bound to complete. The Jade Court's expeditionary force was preparing to march toward Roselia to aid the Dragon Emperor's grand plan, and he had made other arrangements regarding the civil war—he believed the remaining Dragon-kin and the Celestial Court's Guard were sufficient to control the situation. Yuan Bo's apparent indifference to the civil war enraged Yun Xiang beyond measure, and this became the root of the later conflict between the courts.

Over the long years, the Guard's emotions have been worn thin by endless war, yet Miao Yi still harbors feelings for Yun Xiang unlike any other. Her duties and burdens leave her little room to dwell on such things, but she knows—should the situation demand it—she would gladly give her life for him.

The God-Strategy Bureau was once seriously infiltrated by followers of the Sovereign Qing Bao, and even in recent times incidents have occurred where high officials were impersonated. Under Yun Xiang's orders, Miao Yi has repeatedly overseen investigations into the Bureau, even mobilizing the Raven-Feather Legion of the Astronomical Bureau for support, vowing never again to let Chaos's corruption stain the capital.

In the previous invasion of the Dark Elves, Tang Jing Yin, as the Leader of the Martial World, united sects and schools from every corner of Zhen Dan, and at Xuan Yuan won a hard-fought victory that destroyed the Dark Elf coalition seeking to press further inland. Countless heroes, including Tang Jing Yin's own wife, gave their lives for the nation in that battle, and [Giant Hero] himself vanished without a trace after the fighting ended. Now, with the nation's fortunes faltering once more and every common man bearing responsibility, Tang Jing Yin has finally returned to the martial world.

Nearly half of the master warriors of Tang Jing Yin's generation gave their lives in the great battle of Xuan Yuan. When the officials were stretched too thin to act, it was these wandering warriors—once regarded with suspicion by the authorities—who threw themselves before the Celestial Empire's vulnerable flank in service to their country. After the Battle of Xuan Yuan, the Jade Court made an exception and posthumously granted titles to those wandering warriors who had died in battle. Tang Jing Yin, as their leader, was posthumously honored as Duke of Xuan Yuan, but those who had fought at his side, those he had shielded with his own body, called him by another name—the Giant Hero

Tang Jing Yin's era has long passed, yet he still vividly remembers the horrors of the Battle of Xuan Yuan. When the Dark Elf host struck at the moment of weakness along that endless coastline, the Celestial Court's armies were already overwhelmed by Chaos forces pressing in from north and south alike. At Yuan Bo's behest, an emissary from the Jade Court reluctantly convened a martial world assembly, gathering the great heroes of the age. Countless peerless masters vied there for supremacy, and in the end, Tang Jing Yin bested them all, uniting the various sects—each with their own hidden motives—through a stirring speech, persuading these free spirits who cared nothing for matters of state to willingly march toward what might well be a battlefield of no return.
Tang Jingyin belongs to no sect, yet has forged his own style of martial arts through total synthesis, becoming a school unto himself—at that time, none in the world could rival him.

In the Battle of Xuan Yuan, Tang Jing Yin's wife and friends were nearly all slain. Though he drove back the last of the Dark Elves even after losing his left arm in battle, when he searched the battlefield for familiar faces and found only endless corpses, all hope within him shattered. In his despair, this great hero cast himself into the Yu River to end his life, but was unexpectedly saved by the Dragon Monks at the Hao Tian Palace. From then on, he lived in hiding under an assumed name, retreating into the mountains and forests for over a decade.

Zhen Dan enjoyed years of peace after the war, but fate's decree seemed to knock once more upon the gates beyond the heavens—the Dark Elves returned in force, the Jade Blood calamity swept across the Yu River, the Kurgan's hooves trampled the shrouds of fallen frontier soldiers, and the hiss of Serpentmen echoed across the southern border. Though Tang Jing Yin still mourned old wounds, he knew that to turn a blind eye to the suffering of all under heaven would betray the very heart of his chivalry, and would shame the memory of those who gave their lives to defend hearth and home. And so, in this hour of national crisis, the [Giant Hero] has returned.

It is said the Dragon Emperor has sealed himself away in the high towers of the Celestial Court for a century, his blessing withdrawn from the mortal world—but some know that even burdened by his grand design, the Dragon Emperor's gaze still watches over his people. Tang Jing Yin came alone to the Hao Tian Palace, now besieged by the Jade Blood clan, to repay the debt of his rescue long ago, but these unnatural, corrupt abominations once more drove him to the very brink of death. In that final moment, a miracle of Hao Tian descended upon him: the Winds of Magic surged through his body and coalesced into form—he felt an arm long lost to him, and a strength beyond anything he had known. Alone and surrounded, he realized in that instant that dragon and mortal flesh now walked as one.

Tang Jing Yin's return came naturally—he simply did once more what he had done over a decade before: acting with chivalry and righteousness, saving the dying and healing the wounded. From the moment the first person recognized him as the [Giant Hero] of old, word spread like wildfire. Old friends still living and a new generation of wandering warriors who admired his legend were eager to crown him leader of the martial world once more, while others were shocked by the revelation that his death had been faked, and even cast doubt upon the events of that old war—perhaps in some eyes, the giant hero who died for his country was the true hero, and now that he lived, he no longer deserved the title. But regardless of what the world thought, this time, Tang Jing Yin was determined to see his own Wanderer's Code through to the very end.
'Drunk and wandering still, overturning clouds and seas, righteousness stands unshaken'
'Amid ten thousand changes, still unmoved; spirit at ease, mind at peace'
'Ascending beyond the azure sky, soaring ten thousand miles, riding the cool wind, vast and boundless over all things'

Descriptions of the Monkey King vary greatly across the legends of different regions. In the songs of the north, he is a bloodthirsty, raging great ape. In the tales of western storytellers, he is a creature resembling a baboon, with beautiful golden fur and a swollen red rear—for the Monkey King is forever in a fury. In the legends by the eastern shore, this enormous ape has an astonishing appetite, his bare belly covered in unsightly boils. To some in the south, the Monkey King is instead a slight spider-monkey, leaping from shoulder to shoulder among allies and enemies alike, his words a mixture of truth and lies.

In legends from different regions, descriptions of the Monkey King vary widely. In northern ballads, he is a bloodthirsty and savage great ape. In the mouths of western storytellers, he resembles a baboon, with beautiful golden fur and swollen, reddened haunches — for the Monkey King is perpetually enraged. In legends along the eastern coast, this giant ape has an astonishing appetite, his bare belly covered in ugly boils. To some in the south, the Monkey King is instead a slight spider monkey, leaping between the shoulders of allies and enemies alike, his words a mixture of truth and lies.

Day and night, the monkeys of the Simian Court sing praises to the Monkey King: legend tells that even before the Dragon Emperor descended in the age of creation, an immortal stone nurtured by heaven and earth stood atop Mount Tian Shan. One day the stone burst open, birthing a stone egg, which the wind transformed into a stone monkey. When the stone monkey was born, two beams of divine light shot from its eyes, piercing the Dipper's Palace and even stirring the Dragon Emperor in the Celestial Court a thousand li away—and that stone monkey became the one the monkeys of Tian Shan now call the 'Handsome Monkey King.'

The Monkey King lived a carefree, innocent life on Tian Shan for many years, until, seeking the secret of eternal life, he wandered the four seas in search of a master. Though his unmatched natural gifts allowed him to master extraordinary skills, he could never shed his mischievous nature, and was repeatedly expelled from his masters' tutelage for showing off his abilities.

In the year 2377 of the Imperial Calendar, the Monkey King seized control over Zhen Dan. He appointed the Aeshin clan's King Qi Shi Qi as his advisor to establish trade with the Skaven. The Dragon-kin, at last understanding the old wisdom that brothers must set aside their quarrels to face outside threats, turned as one to oppose this self-proclaimed usurper's monkey head.

Calling the Simian Court a 'court' may be something of a stretch, for the Monkey King and his subjects rarely do anything so orderly as hold formal assemblies. Yet as with the Tiger Warrior's court, some still hope the Monkey King might discipline the monkey soldiers under his command the way the Dragon-kin govern the people of Zhen Dan. In practice, the Simian Court's assemblies invariably descend into chaos. While the Monkey King smugly believes his rule rivals that of any Dragon-kin, the rest of Zhen Dan can only watch in stunned disbelief at the shambles his kingdom has become.

'After that battle at the Celestial Court, though the Monkey King narrowly escaped the pursuit of the Dragon Sons back to Mount Tian Shan, he could not escape the Dragon Emperor's sight: the Five Elements Compass, a thousand li away, thundered without end, churning the very contours of Tian Shan. As the monkeys scattered like startled birds amid the dust, the Monkey King was astonished to find himself trapped within the confines of solid rock. The Dragon Emperor's voice rose within his mind: though the Monkey King is not evil by nature, and his mischief in Zhen Dan brought no great disaster, the peace of Zhen Dan has nonetheless been shattered by his hand, and his incorrigible nature will one day give destructive forces an opening to exploit. The Dragon Emperor shall punish him—but this, too, is his chance: one day in the future, a pilgrim traveling west shall pass through Tian Shan, and on that day the Monkey King's chains shall be broken, and his true purpose shall begin...'

The monkeys stormed into Wei Jing amid the chaos, and the Monkey King himself soared straight up into the clouds, wreaking havoc upon the Celestial Court itself. The heroes who guarded the Dragon Emperor's palace, proud above all under heaven, were led on a merry chase by the mischievous monkey. The stern and silent Palace Guard cursed aloud at his endless tricks, and even Yun Xiang, the mightiest champion beneath the Dragon Emperor, could do nothing to stop him. Only when the allied Dragon armies were mere steps from the capital did the Monkey King finally gather his followers and flee in a panic.
'One becomes ten, ten becomes a hundred, and the transformations of hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, millions — all are the arts of Body Outside the Body.'

The Monkey King forged his body from the stolen peaches of immortality, the imperial wine, and the dragon elixirs, tempered together in samadhi fire. Blade and axe, thunder and flame, poison and liquor — none of it leaves so much as a scratch.

Though the Monkey King learned the art of immortality from the Old Immortal of Tian Shan, only by surviving the 'Three Calamities' could he achieve true eternal life! After his desperate pleading, the Old Immortal finally taught him the Seventy-Two Transformations, allowing him to escape the harm of heavenly thunder, dark fire, and the crushing wind — thus fulfilling his wish for immortality.
Gathering form, dispersing qi, leaving neither trace nor track.
A wondrous art of manipulation — with but a single point of the finger, the enemy is pinned in place, unable to move.

Na Tian was once the Third Prince of Zhu Long's court. As a pure-blooded descendant of Zhu Long, he was as untamed and headstrong as Li Dao, and greatly favored by Zhu Long, but his willful temperament eventually brought disaster—an envoy delegation from the Ming Dragon was so enraged by the arrogant Na Tian that a conflict broke out, and in the chaos Na Tian accidentally killed a Dragon-Kin of Yin Yin. Knowing he had caused a grave catastrophe, Na Tian, to spare Ling Nan from being implicated, cut the flesh from his own bones and ended his own life. The grieving Zhu Long sent his remains to Kun Lan, where the Old Immortal preserved Na Tian's soul through the wondrous art of Lotus Incarnation. Since then, Na Tian has cultivated under the Old Immortal as his attendant disciple, hoping one day to atone for his past mistakes with future merit.

Na Tian's mortal flesh perished a hundred years ago; his current form is merely an avatar shaped through wondrous arts by the Old Immortal of Kun Lan at that time — yet it possesses undying, indestructible power, capable of infinite transformation.

As a pure-blooded descendant of Zhu Long, Nanuo Tian's temperament resembles his father's more closely than any of his siblings, and he has inherited that same peerless divine power, earning him Li Dao's deep favor. The people call him the Third Prince of Ling Nan.
Eyes Open, Wrath; Eyes Closed, Ruin

Nanuo Tian spent his days as crown prince in idle splendor, but his willful temper eventually brought disaster. When a delegation from the Ming Long court paraded through the streets with such arrogance toward the common folk that it vexed the Third Prince, he subjected them to endless mischief. Unexpectedly, the Dragon-kin flew into a rage, and both sides came to blows—the enraged Third Prince flayed that dragon-kin alive by the canal. By the time he came to his senses, disaster had already struck.
The Sword in Fire Cuts the Neck

Wracked with regret, Nanuo Tian stumbled back to Zhu Long's estate, only to find crowds already gathering behind him—the Ming Long envoy had brought the assembled Dragon-kin to demand justice. With no way to settle the debt and desperate to spare Li Dao's court any entanglement, Nanuo Tian drew his blade before Zhu Long's estate and cut his own throat. As the spraying blood arced through the air, it was instantly boiled away by the Sash of Chaos-Rending wrapped about his body, which flickered out along with his life.
As the Wind Stills, the Soul Drifts

In his grief, Zhu Long carried the Third Prince's body away, seeking only some means to restore his life: the Mother of Rebirth at the Vermilion Bird Temple shook her head—the pure-blooded vessel had already burned away all its vitality. The Old Immortal of Tian Shan exhausted every elixir and miracle drug, yet no fragment of his spirit returned. At last, Zhu Long journeyed to Kun Lan, for the Old Immortal there had once served as the Dragon Emperor's chancellor and received a golden token from Hao Tian himself—if any mortal being could still perform a miracle beyond the reach of the Dragon-kin, it was he. The Old Immortal of Kun Lan shaped a new form for Nanuo Tian using the Lotus Incarnation technique, then drew his soul back with the power of the Winds of Magic. Once the incense had circulated fully through this new vessel, the Third Prince returned to life. Li Dao departed Kun Lan the day before Nanuo Tian's return, leaving only word for the Old Immortal to take the Third Prince as his disciple thereafter, that he might one day atone for his past sins.
Half a Scroll Read, All Frost and Wind Traversed

From the moment of his rebirth, no one has ever again called Nanuo Tian the Third Prince, and he has never returned to Ling Nan nor seen Zhu Long again. He cultivated diligently under the Old Immortal of Kun Lan for a hundred years, and after his master ascended to the immortal realm, he journeyed to the Celestial Court, fighting without rest ever since. Perhaps his sins have long since been absolved—may he one day find his way home.

Nanuo Tian cultivated atop Kun Lan for a hundred years, until the outbreak of the civil war drew him down from the mountain once more. He accompanied the Old Immortal of Kun Lan in aiding the generals of the God-Strategy Bureau. None knew who this fiery young man was, but all marveled that the Old Immortal's disciples were uniformly extraordinary, and appointed him their vanguard general.
'One becomes ten, ten becomes a hundred, and the transformations of hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, millions — all are the arts of Body Outside the Body.'

Though mortal in flesh, their valor rivals that of the Dragon-Kin, their strength capable of moving mountains, unstoppable upon the battlefield.

A peerless warrior sweeps the battlefield unopposed, one against a thousand. When they unleash their full strength, no enemy can withstand the blow.

Yi Qing is fierce and valiant, bold and resourceful beyond compare. He shattered the Kurgan, opened up the northern frontier, cleared the realm of turmoil, and brought peace to the Celestial land. His strategies are peerless, unmatched by any hero of Cathay.
The people of Cathay have long recorded history through poetry. This scroll records the works of countless poets across Cathay's millennia. Yi Qing, being fond of learning, carries it with him always

Having pacified the northern frontier, Yi Qing drove the rampaging forces of Chaos back into the depths of the desert, leading countless nomadic peoples who had fled Zhen Dan back to their homelands to rebuild.

As one of the Nine Venerables of Nan Gao, Qiao Xiao holds an unshakeable position there. He is the master swordsmith of the Artisans' Guild, and the nobles of the Wei Bei provinces treasure the blades he forges as priceless heirlooms — though Qiao Xiao himself scorns such vanity: the weapons he forges are meant to slay Zhen Dan's enemies, not to be admired as ornaments in a hall.

Qiao Xiao has forged several blades known as 'Nan Gao's Peerless Sky,' legendary weapons of the current age rivaling even the Six Swords of Kun Lan in renown. Save for the Clear Melting Sword, all the others are kept locked within a case, never leaving his side.

The Stone-Burning Spike is Qiao Xiao's forging tool, crafted from otherworldly materials and tempered in the fires of the southern flame. This tool alone is the finest proof of Qiao Xiao's mastery of the forge

Xin Qi is unstoppable on the battlefield, as if the New Martial Marquis had returned to the world

A tiger-shaped talisman stone issued by the Bin Xi court during Ye Sheng's tenure as General Who Quells the Barbarians, ensuring his authority to command the heavy garrisons of the western frontier against rampaging ogres and border unrest. The tiger-shaped talisman stone issued by the Bin Xi court when Ye Sheng served as General Who Breaks the Barbarians, to ensure he could mobilize the heavy troops of the western frontier against rebellious ogres and border raiders. Ye Sheng carried it to protect the frontier—and carried it also to overthrow Shang Yang.

Though the Ogre Wars ended long ago, hordes of Ogres still band together with tribesmen from Cathay's western frontier to launch raids. Ye Sheng, thanks to his exceptional political skill, was chosen to suppress the unrest — and his string of victories in the west proved he was no mere schemer of court intrigue. The Bin Xi court granted him the title General Who Shatters the Invader, and he held the border with his own private army. Later, when Dong Yan led the gentry rebels in revolt, Ye Sheng immediately marched back to Shang Yang, and together with Xin Qi and Feng Yao, plotted to kill the usurper Dong Yan. The three swore to jointly hold the reins of Shang Yang's court until the Eighth-Generation Lord of Shang Yang returned north to the throne. But Ye Sheng's ambitions did not end there — with promises of gain, he lured Feng Yao into joining him to surround and kill Xin Qi, who refused to take part in a second rebellion. He then seized control of Shang Yang's forces, scheming to claim the entire western provinces of Cathay and carve out his own kingdom.

When the curse of the Jade Blood Clan fell upon the Nong Chang basin, Jin Xiao, the leader of the Protector Guard, could not escape the nightmare of undeath either. Perhaps through sheer force of will, an extraordinary constitution, or simple luck, Jin Xiao — his flesh dissolved to bone — retained his mind intact, and continued to wear the Protector's mask, leading the survivors of Nong Chang against the Jade Blood Clan. With the arrival of the Jade Dragon, the crisis of Nong Chang was temporarily averted, but Yuan Bo also uncovered Jin Xiao's secret. Contrary to Jin Xiao's own expectation of death, Yuan Bo used his mighty sorcery to transform Jin Xiao's body — his shattered bones reformed into jade, and the power contained within left even Jin Xiao in disbelief. The Jade Dragon then moved on as he always did, and Jin Xiao does not know whether this act stemmed from trust, mercy, or mere curiosity — but whatever the reason, he will not let his second life go to waste.
